lines: A live race's result now belongs to the service: places, times and output nobody's browser can change.
The race ends when every rider has finished or dropped out, or two minutes after the first one finished.
The service records each place, time and output from the progress it saw, and a submitted ride takes them from there.
Finish before the result is in, and Results says it is recording; the app asks again every five seconds.
Once the service has it, the XP arrives, from a phone to the full screen.
What the tests prove: the service's place wins, the race ends on time, and the app waits for it.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
